result.reason: Section (c) reaches the preferred T4C position: Company may terminate an outstanding SOW or the Agreement on 30 days’ written notice without a fee, pays only for performed Services, receives a refund of prepaid fees for unperformed Services, and Contractor cannot terminate for convenience while a SOW is uncompleted. Contractor’s retained 15-day right under Section (a) applies only when no SOW is outstanding, so it does not operate during a committed engagement. However, new Section (b) unnecessarily adds and modifies unrelated breach-termination, payment, and work-in-progress assignment provisions, including a broad IP assignment. The overlap between Sections (a) and (c) also gives Company different notice periods depending on whether a SOW is outstanding and could be clarified. Thus, the redline is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated commercial intent.
